title: The fraction cocone is colimiting
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, A its valuation ring and varpi the recorded uniformizer. Let X be any scheme. Use the continuous coefficient sheaves, scalar maps, normalized towers and quotient predicate of [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data]. The cocone from repeated multiplication by l on the integral coefficient unit, with point the restricted field coefficient unit and legs a maps to l^(-n) a, is colimiting in sheaf A_X-modules.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text:
for a continuous field-valued function f, the inverse images of the open
sets l^(-m) A cover its domain. On the m-th member f is represented by the
integral function l^m f at the m-th stage. These local fractions agree after
passing to a common higher stage. A cocone from the multiplication diagram
therefore defines a unique map from the field coefficient unit, by gluing its
values on these representatives. Independence follows because A embeds in E
and l is nonzero, so two equal fractions become equal integral functions at a
common stage. This also proves additivity and integral linearity, checked on
common refinements, and compatibility with restriction. Applying the cocone
identities to integral fractions gives the factorization property. Every section
is locally a fraction, so sheaf uniqueness proves uniqueness of the factorization.
The construction includes empty objects.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4(1), coefficient and local-basis arguments
